filesystem.read.description: Inspect files and directories without changing them.

filesystem.write.description: Create and modify files and directories inside the workspace.
filesystem.write.note: Every path is confined to the workspace root, including through symlinks.

search.description: Search file contents and file names as cancellable sessions.

process.description: Run commands, either to completion or as interactive background sessions.
process.note: Commands run in a shell, so this group can reach capabilities other groups gate. It is policy controlled.

git.default_policy: mixed: inspection is allowed, mutation needs approval

network.note: Requests to loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, and private addresses are refused by the runtime.

introspection.description: Inspect what the runtime itself has executed.

planning.description: Keep the plan and its progress on disk so work survives the end of a run.
planning.note: The plan is the agent's own bookkeeping inside the workspace, so it is not treated as a destructive write.

memory.description: Read the working memory and retrieve archived events from earlier in this run or from previous runs.
memory.note: Retrieval is selective: search returns titles and previews, and only archive_get loads a body into the conversation.

knowledge.description: Load the procedures the runtime knows, when they are needed.
knowledge.note: Skills are instructions, not operations, so reading one changes nothing outside the conversation.

code.query.description: Query the semantic code index: symbols, dependencies, summaries, search, impact, tests, and config.

code.index.description: Manage semantic index generation lifecycle sessions.

code.live.description: Live compiler and language server operations: diagnostics, call hierarchy, definition, organize imports.

code.write.description: Compiler-backed safe code refactorings across the workspace.

mcp.inspect.description: See which MCP servers are connected and what tools they offer.
mcp.inspect.note: Reading the catalogue contacts a server but never asks it to do anything.

mcp.call.description: Call a tool on an MCP server, either through the gateway or by its mcp__<server>__<tool> name.
mcp.call.note: What a server tool actually does is outside this runtime, so the workspace boundary does not cover it. A server marked restricted needs approval for every call.
mcp.call.default_policy: mixed: allowed by default, require_approval for a restricted server

mcp.manage.description: Connect and disconnect MCP servers while the runtime is running.
mcp.manage.note: Adding a server grants capabilities this runtime did not ship with, and a stdio server is a process this runtime starts.

discussion.description: Run a structured multi-agent discussion: specialist personas deliberate in rounds and an observer decides when to finish and writes the final synthesis.
discussion.note: Personas reason, they do not act on the workspace, so no approval is needed; the cost is in model calls, bounded by max_rounds.
